raw_response:
I am not going to spread myself too thin this year. On my 12.4 mu, I will keep the old way that feels steady: wheat-maize on most of the land, and cotton on the rest. I have done this many years. Wheat and maize keep grain coming and are safer for the household, and cotton gives me some cash if the price is decent. I only finished primary school, so I do not calculate too fancy. I look at what happened on my own fields and what the neighbors are doing. Last year the wheat did better where I did not save too much on base fertilizer, and maize needs to go in fast after wheat harvest, so I will leave enough money and labor for that tight turn. Water from the well costs money, so I will irrigate at the important times, not too many times.

For the wheat-maize land, I will use 8.4 mu. Wheat goes in first in October, then maize goes in right after wheat harvest in June. On the other 4.0 mu I will plant cotton in spring. Some people in the family work outside, so I cannot depend on everyone being home at the right time. I will use family labor first and only hire a little help if harvest or cotton picking gets tight. I would rather put a bit more fertilizer than too little on wheat, because if wheat turns yellow later it is hard to recover. But I still need to keep cash in hand, so I am not chasing the highest yield, just a steady one.
